items.title: Revised Achievement Standards and supporting materials for assessment in 2027 11/09/2026 Available now for planning purposes.
items.summary: Available now for planning purposes.
items.readerText:
A number of NCEA assessment materials have been updated for 2027 following the 2026 Review and Maintenance of NCEA. Teachers and other NCEA providers must ensure that all assessment in 2026 continues to use the current 2026 versions of Achievement Standards and supporting materials. A number of NCEA assessment materials have been updated for 2027 following the 2026 Review and Maintenance Programme. The Level 3 Te Ao Haka Achievement Standards, along with one Achievement Standard for Level 2 Economics (91227), have been updated during this process; the other updates have been made to assessment supporting materials. All updated NCEA materials for New Zealand Curriculum (NZC) are now available for 2027 planning purposes on the NCEA.Education website.

Draft External Assessment Specifications for 2027 will be available on the NZQA website.

NZC: The updates are available as PDFs, organised by subject, on the NCEA Support page. These are watermarked as “For Planning 2027”.

Te Marautanga o Aotearoa: Kaupae 2 and 3 Toi Puoro supporting materials and Tikanga Aromatawai for all subjects will be available on the NCEA Support page in Term 4.

The updated content is for use from 2027. In January 2027, the updated materials will replace the current materials on the NCEA.Education website for NZC Level 1 and Te Ao Haka Level 3; for NZC Levels 2 and 3, the materials will be updated on the TKI website. Once this has happened, the PDFs will be removed from NCEA.Education.

The Level 3 Te Ao Haka Achievement Standards and Level 2 Economics Achievement Standard (91227) that have been updated and are hosted on NZQA’s website will also be updated in January.

items.title: Te Poutāhū Curriculum Centre school update · 5 August 2026
items.summary: The latest curriculum, assessment, and aromatawai news for schools and kura.
items.readerText:
The New Zealand School Property Agency (NZSPA) has been established as a Crown entity, to manage, plan, build, maintain and administer the education property portfolio. More information – NZSPA

The latest curriculum, assessment, and aromatawai news for schools and kura.

As we begin a new term, we acknowledge the significant progress across kura and schools as updated curriculum, assessment, and teaching supports move into everyday practice.

This update brings together recent announcements, newly available resources, and key updates to support your planning and practice for the term ahead.

Below you’ll find key highlights and links to Tāhūrangi to help you focus on what matters most for ākonga.

Te Tāhuhu o te Mātauranga | Ministry of Education

Years 0 to 10 curriculum release dates announced #

Last month, we announced that the final frameworks and Years 0 to 10 content for the New Zealand Curriculum (NZC) and Te Marautanga o Aotearoa (TMoA) will be published by Wednesday 9 September 2026.

The considerable participation in the Years 0 to 10 curriculum consultation led to nearly 3,900 submissions on the drafts, so we’ve taken some extra time to make sure all feedback is considered carefully.

At the same time, we will publish “What you told us and how we responded” reports, which will summarise the feedback we received during the consultation and explain how we responded to it. We did this for English, Mathematics and Statistics, Te Reo Rangatira and Pāngarau.

We are also releasing some content earlier – Science and Social Sciences (12 August), and Pūtaiao and Pūmanawa Tangata (26 August) – to help schools and kura get ready to start using it from the start of 2027.

Years 0 to 10 curriculum release dates – Tāhūrangi

You can direct queries to either of the below.

Phonics Checks – corrections to students records and assessment materials #

Earlier this year, the Phonics Checks tool was updated so that all checks are stopped after 5 consecutive word errors, in keeping with administration guidance. For previously completed checks that continued past this point, the results were recalculated and corrected in student records on 21 May. The student results now showing in the tool are the correct and final record.

Additionally, we recently updated Phonics Checks student materials for Terms 2, 3 and 4. These updates include corrections to minor errors such as the incorrect labelling of ‘real’ words and ‘pseudo’ words. The errors did not affect the accuracy of any assessments previously completed, and do not need to be redone.

You can access the latest materials for upcoming Phonics Checks on Tāhūrangi.

Phonics Checks: assessment materials – Tāhūrangi

Updated resources: Tāhūrangi improvements #

We've made some changes to the NZC and TMoA homepages on Tāhūrangi. The new page layouts have been designed based on your feedback and make it easier for you to find the resources you need.

We’ve recently updated the leadership resources section on Tāhūrangi – NZC with new resource categories. We’ve also relocated all resources from the implementation supports section to these new categories. For example, 2025 and 2026 roadshow resources can now be found under 'Change Leadership and Implementation Resources'.

Opening soon: Year 7 and 8 Maths Acceleration Programme and Hāpai Pāngarau Tau 7 and 8 #

Applications for Cohorts 1, 2, and 3 of the Maths and Pāngarau Acceleration Programmes in 2027 will open on 10 August. Applications will close on 4 September, and outcomes will be notified by 18 September.

More information about the programmes, funding, and process is available on Tāhūrangi.

Maths and Pāngarau Years 7 and 8 intervention – Tāhūrangi

Register now: professional learning and development opportunities #

A range of professional learning and development (PLD) opportunities are currently available to support teachers, kaiako, leaders and tumuaki as they implement the refreshed curriculum and strengthen teaching, learning and assessment practice.

We encourage early registration where applicable, as places may be limited.

Applications for the second round open on 3 August and close on 21 August. This PLD is designed to strengthen the assessment and aromatawai capabilities of teachers, kaiako, leaders and tumuaki.

Curriculum workshops and webinars support implementation across learning areas.

Mathematics and Statistics Years 9 to 10

Te Poipoi Kaiako | Mentor Support Programme workshops

These are available both online and across Aotearoa New Zealand, supporting Mentor Teachers and Provisionally Certificated Teachers.

Te Poipoi Kaiako | Mentor Support Programme workshops – Core Education

Coming soon: Teacher Support Materials for Wharekura #

From week 3 in Term 3, the following will be available on Tāhūrangi:

These curated te reo Māori texts integrate mātauranga Māori and Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics, supporting the teaching of Te Reo Rangatira and Pūtaiao in wharekura. The new support materials will help kaiako use these high-quality secondary curriculum resources in their teaching programmes.

Three new School Journals are being sent to schools and kura at the beginning of August.

Each journal includes engaging stories, articles, plays, and poems designed to support literacy learning and reflect the lives of New Zealand students. The themes for these journals are space exploration (Year 4), future proofing (Years 5 and 6), and wellbeing (Years 7 and 8).

New Teacher Support Materials (TSMs) will be available on Tāhūrangi. The TSMs have a new structure and content designed to align with the refreshed English learning area and structured literacy approaches.

Teaching resources to support structured literacy approaches – Tāhūrangi

What’s coming up for SMART Assessment Window 2 #

We're continuing to improve SMART ahead of Assessment Window 2, informed by feedback from schools and kura. We will share more detail closer to the opening of Assessment Window 2, but the changes include:

new self-service options that enable teachers to manage key tasks within SMART

an improved scanning process for all paper-based assessments

further development of reporting, including comparison of a student’s results between Assessment 1 and Assessment 2, and reporting to support combined classes (for example, Year 3 and Year 4 in 1 classroom).

If you have feedback on your experience during SMART Assessment Window 1, we'd love to hear from you.

SMART Assessment Window 1: Your feedback

Your feedback will help shape future guidance, assessment content, reporting, and platform improvements. We’re particularly interested in hearing about:

the guidance, training, and support that would help your school or kura get the most value from SMART

which parts of SMART reporting you found most useful

what additional information or insights would support teaching and learning.

As always, if you have any questions, email us.

items.title: Updates to 2026 Assessment Specifications - A2026/2
items.summary: An Assessment Matters newsletter about 2026 Assessment Specifications.
items.readerText:
Assessment specifications provide the annual assessment parameters for each externally assessed achievement standard and New Zealand Scholarship performance standard. They must be read alongside the applicable standards.

The assessment specifications for subjects externally assessed by examinations include the:

context for questions, where appropriate.

For the submitted portfolios or reports, they include the:

portfolio/report specifications, including the type and volume of materials that may be submitted as evidence.

Some 2026 assessment specifications have recently been updated to provide further clarification of the requirements and conditions of the assessment.

The following Scholarship subjects have amended assessment specifications to reflect the option of a candidate being able take the examination digitally:

The following subjects have had a change of submission date:

Technology, Level 2 and Level 3 changed to 28 October 2026

Visual Arts, Level 3 and Scholarship changed to 2 November 2026

Other assessment specifications have amendments, as follows:

Design and Visual Communication, Level 1, 92002, 92003

Design and Visual Communication, Level 2, 91337, 91338, 91339

Design and Visual Communication, Level 3, 91627

Digital Technologies, Scholarship, 93604

New Zealand Sign Language, Level 1, 92357, 92358

Technology, Level 2, 91358, 91359, 91360, 91363

Technology, Level 3, 91612, 91613, 91614, 91617

Visual Arts, Level 2, 91320, 91321, 91322, 91323, 91324

Visual Arts, Level 3, 91455, 91456, 91457, 91458, 91459

Visual Arts, Scholarship, 93306, 93307, 93308, 93309, 93310

Visual Arts Sculpture (Level 3 and NZ Scholarship)

In 2025, NZQA conducted a live trial with Level 3 and NZ Scholarship Sculpture to determine the feasibility of submitting digitally and assessing the material digitally. The trial was a valuable learning experience for NZQA and in that respect we can consider the trial a success. The trial uncovered a range of nuanced complexities that will need to be carefully worked through before a digital submission is re-introduced.

The 2026 submission process for Level 3 and Scholarship Sculpture will, therefore, revert back to the physical portfolio submission process used up to 2024. The assessment method has now been updated in the assessment specifications.

2026 Tautuhinga Aromatawai (Assessment Specifications)

There are no further updates to these. The final versions can be found on the subject pages.

items.title: Special Assessment Conditions (SAC) Notification Gateway - A2026/1
items.summary: Special Assessment Conditions (SAC) Notification Gateway
items.readerText:
Special Assessment Conditions (SAC) Notification Gateway

NZQA has completed a review of SAC processes and has introduced several changes from 2026, including an expansion of the Notifications Gateway. The updated system will simplify SAC applications while ensuring decisions remain evidence-based and aligned with the needs of students/ākonga.

When making new SAC applications for students/ākonga undertaking assessment of standards listed in the Directory of Assessment and Skill Standards, schools can choose either the Approvals Gateway to submit applications for NZQA approval, or the Notifications Gateway to inform NZQA of student/ākonga needs and the SAC required.

The Notifications Gateway has moved beyond the trial phase and is now available for Years 11–13.

Applications through the Notifications Gateway pathway do not require NZQA approval or the submission of evidence at the time of application.

Schools must still retain robust evidence for every SAC decision, as NZQA will audit notifications made through the Notifications Gateway.

The Approvals Gateway continues for cases requiring additional guidance or where complex support needs are identified.

identify students/ākonga with learning, medical, sensory or physical difficulties that impact on fair assessment, and to determine what SAC support is appropriate.

design inclusive environments influenced by knowledge of students/ākonga.

discuss the option of SAC with students/ākonga and their whānau.

gather and retain evidence of students/ākonga needs.

use one of the gateways to tell NZQA what SAC students require.

monitor students/ākonga progress and trial supports as needed.

items.title: Outcomes of the 2025 biennial consultation on the New Zealand Scholarship subject list - A2025/15
items.summary: Assessment Matters newsletter 2025/15
items.readerText:
Outcomes of the 2025 biennial consultation on the New Zealand Scholarship subject list (the List)

Every two years, NZQA consults with the education sector and other interested groups about the subjects assessed in New Zealand Scholarship.

NZQA sought feedback between 12 June and 11 July 2025 on subjects to be included on, or excluded from, the List from 2027. Feedback was not sought on any specific subject. Respondents could free-type the subjects they wanted to provide feedback on, rather than selecting from a pre-populated list.

Go to the current Scholarship subject list

The biennial review aims to maintain the credibility of Scholarship by ensuring subjects:

are relevant and meet government and sector expectations

can be administered effectively and efficiently, and

have sufficient workforce supply to support quality assessment at the appropriate level.

How New Zealand Scholarship subjects are selected

three supported splitting Health and Physical into two separate subjects.

Agribusiness, Business Studies and Social Studies had 11, 15 and 1 submission respectively in support of their inclusion.

All feedback was considered, and each subject was assessed against the criteria for inclusion. The inclusion of Lea Faka Tonga was also reconsidered.

The following outcomes were endorsed by NZQA’s Technical Overview Group Assessment and agreed by the NZQA Board:

Health and Physical Education to remain as a single subject.

Agribusiness is not added to the list at this time.

Business Studies is added to the list from 2027.

Social Studies is not added to the list at this time.

Lea Faka Tonga is not added to the list at this time.

The next review is planned for 2027, to determine subjects for inclusion or exclusion from 2029.

Note: 2025 is the final year that Scholarship Latin will be offered.

Please refer any enquiries relating to this circular to your School Relationship Manager.
